chosen.title: Inverted SKULLCRUSHERS
chosen.description:
💥 Build Tricep Power with Inverted Skullcrushers at We, The Collective Fitness! 💥

The Inverted Skullcrusher is a twist on the traditional tricep exercise, utilizing a barbell set in a rack at a fixed height to create a bodyweight version of this classic move. This exercise is ideal for building #TricepStrength while engaging your core, shoulders, and stability muscles. At We, The Collective Fitness (WTCF), our trainers ensure you get the most out of this dynamic exercise with proper form and progression.

How to Perform Inverted Skullcrushers (WTCF):
Set the Bar:

Position a barbell in a squat rack at about hip height. This will act as the base for the movement.
Grip the Bar:

Stand in front of the barbell and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms down), hands shoulder-width apart.
Step Back:

Walk your feet back so your body is at an angle to the ground, keeping your arms straight and your body in a plank-like position. Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower Your Forehead to the Bar:

Keeping your elbows tucked in, slowly bend your elbows and lower your forehead toward the bar, similar to a traditional skullcrusher motion. Your triceps should do the majority of the work, with minimal assistance from your core and back muscles.
Press Back Up:

Once your head is just above the bar, press through your triceps to extend your arms back to the starting position. Control the movement and avoid rushing through it.
Repeat:

Complete your set by maintaining strict form and smooth, controlled movements.
Benefits of Inverted Skullcrushers (WTCF):
#TricepStrength: This move directly targets the triceps, building mass and strength.
#CoreStability: Engages your core throughout the exercise to keep your body stable and aligned.
#JointFriendly: A great alternative for those who experience discomfort with traditional weighted skullcrushers, as the angle reduces stress on the elbows.
#Scalable: You can adjust the difficulty by altering the bar height or your foot placement.
Trainer Tips for Inverted Skullcrushers (WTCF):
Engage Your Core: Keep your body in a straight line by engaging your core and glutes throughout the movement. Avoid sagging hips or arching your back.
Adjust Difficulty: To make the movement easier, raise the bar or move your feet closer. To increase difficulty, lower the bar or step your feet further back.
Control the Eccentric Phase: Focus on the lowering part of the movement (eccentric phase) to maximize tricep engagement and control.
Take your tricep workout to the next level with Inverted Skullcrushers at We, The Collective Fitness (WTCF)! It's a fantastic variation to add strength, definition, and functional movement to your tricep routine. 💪 #InvertedSkullcrushers #WTCF #BodyweightTriceps #TricepStrength #FunctionalTraining

candidates.title: STOP doing SKULLCRUSHERS like This!
candidates.description:
The skullcrusher is a great exercise to develop the long head of the tricep, but oftentimes, it isn't carried out as efficiently as it could be. Since the long head of the tricep originates from the scapula, this means that it assists in shoulder extension/flexion. When you lower the weight directly overhead, you not only limit the range of motion, but you also reduce the tension on your triceps, since there isn't as much shoulder flexion as there could be. So instead, bring the bar back and lower the weight behind your head, so that your elbows drift back and your shoulders extend past 90 degrees of flexion which will optimally engage the long head and lead to more growth.

Try it out and let me know how it goes. #Shorts #Gym

candidates.description:
Maximize your Dumbbell Skullcrushers ⚠️
.
Form Tip #1: When Setting Up for the Movement, Make Sure the Dumbbells are on your Knees so you can Kick the Dumbbells Back into Position. ✅

Form Tip #2: Make sure when you Descend the Weight Down your Hands are in a Neutral Position. ✅

Form Tip #3: Keep your Chest Up and Flex your Lats Slightly to have a Stabilize Harder into Position. ✅

Form Tip #4: Make Sure your Knees are Out and Squeeze your Glutes in Together for Greater Stability in your Lower Body. ✅

Form Tip #5: Lastly, instead of Having your Shoulders Positioned at 90DEGs, Slightly Shift your Shoulders Back so you can get a Full Stretch in your Triceps at the Bottom. ✅

candidates.description:

candidates.title: Skull crushers
candidates.description:
Get the most from Skull crushers in 6 easy steps 👇🏽

Incline bench skull crushers are a variation of the traditional skull crusher exercise that specifically target the upper portion of the triceps muscle. Here are some tips to maximize the effectiveness of this exercise:

Set up the bench at the appropriate angle: The incline bench should be set at a 45-degree angle. This angle will allow you to target the upper portion of the triceps muscle effectively.

Use an appropriate weight: Choose a weight that allows you to perform 8-12 reps with good form. If you can’t perform at least 8 reps, the weight is too heavy, and if you can perform more than 12 reps, the weight is too light.

Keep your elbows stationary: Throughout the exercise, make sure your elbows remain stationary and close to your head. This will ensure that the focus remains on the triceps muscle.
Lower the weight slowly: As you lower the weight towards your head, do so slowly and with control. This will increase the time under tension on the triceps muscle, leading to greater muscle activation and growth.

Squeeze at the top: As you extend your arms back up towards the starting position, squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement. This will further activate the muscle and enhance the effectiveness of the exercise.

Use different grip positions: You can vary the grip position on the barbell or dumbbells to target different areas of the triceps muscle. For example, a narrower grip will target the medial head of the triceps, while a wider grip will target the lateral head.

By following these tips, you can maximize the effectiveness of incline bench skull crushers and achieve greater triceps muscle activation and growth.

candidates.title: ✅ The Perfect Lying Triceps Extension (DO THIS!)
candidates.description:
Perfect Lying Triceps Extension Form Tips

1) Use a Thumbless Grip: A thumbless (or "suicide") grip positions the bar closer to the base of your palm, reducing wrist strain and making it easier to keep your elbows tucked. A full grip (with thumbs wrapped around the bar) isn't necessarily wrong, but it often causes elbows to flare, which can compromise form (as discussed in the next point).

2) Tuck Your Elbows: Keep your elbows tucked throughout the entire movement. Flaring them out increases the risk of elbow pain and activates your shoulders and chest, turning the exercise into a partial chest fly rather than isolating the triceps.

3) Angle Your Upper Arms Slightly Back: Position your upper arms at a slight backward angle instead of vertically straight. This improves the range of motion by allowing you to lower the bar further behind your head, maximizing the triceps stretch. It also ensures the triceps remain engaged at the top of the movement. Keeping your upper arms vertical reduces the range of motion (as the bar can only lower to your forehead) and minimizes triceps tension when your arms are fully extended.
